Biological neurons communicate sparingly using binary spikes, contrasting with the continuous-valued activations of artificial networks. Artificial Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) can be constructed by replacing ANN units with spiking neurons. Current SNNs perform far below deep ANNs on challenging benchmarks. These SNNs use much higher firing rates compared to biological counterparts, which limits their efficiency gains. We demonstrate how spiking neurons employing efficient neural coding can construct SNNs matching high-performance ANNs. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art SNN results on important benchmarks while requiring lower average firing rates. Spike-time coding based on firing rate limiting adaptation phenomenon provides the foundation for our method. This adaptation phenomenon occurs naturally in biological spiking neurons. Adapting spiking neuron models can capture this phenomenon mathematically. We derive the effective transfer function for these adaptive neuron models. ANNs trained with this transfer function allow direct substitution with adaptive spiking neurons. The resulting Adaptive SNNs (AdSNNs) perform inference in deep neural networks using up to an order of magnitude fewer spikes than previous SNNs. Adaptive spike-time coding enables dynamic control of neural coding precision during operation. A simple arousal model in AdSNNs further halves the average required firing rate beyond baseline improvements. This arousal concept naturally extends to other forms of attention mechanisms in neural networks. AdSNNs represent a novel and efficient model for neural computation with strong theoretical foundations. The architecture naturally fits temporally continuous applications where timing matters. Asynchronous processing becomes feasible with this event-driven computational framework. The energy efficiency gains make AdSNNs promising for neuromorphic hardware implementations.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::33: Context. LQ Hya is one of the most frequently studied young solar analogue stars. Between 2003 and 2009, observations revealed a coherent spot structure migrating in the rotational frame, as documented by various authors. Since that time, the star has entered a chaotic state where coherent structures seem to have disappeared. Rapid phase jumps of the photometric minima now occur irregularly over time. Aims. The SOFIN/FIES long-term monitoring campaign has tracked LQ Hya for 25 years. We present new temperature maps for the star covering the period 2006--2017. These maps document the chaotic state of the star. Methods. We employ a Doppler imaging technique to derive surface temperature maps from high-resolution spectra. Results. The mean temperatures extracted from the Doppler maps reveal a weak but systematic increase in the surface temperature of the star. This temperature rise is consistent with the simultaneously increasing photometric magnitude. During nearly all observing seasons we detect a high-latitude spot structure which is clearly nonaxisymmetric. The phase behaviour of this structure is very chaotic but agrees reasonably well with the photometry. Equatorial spots are also frequently seen in our observations. Many of these equatorial spots we interpret to be artefacts due to the poor to moderate phase coverage. Conclusions. The spot topology has remained very similar to the higher activity epochs even during the chaotic phase. Higher activity epochs featured more coherent and long-lived spot structures than currently observed. High-latitude and equatorial spot activity continue to characterize the star. The mid latitude range still being most often void of spots, as in previous epochs. We attribute the erratic jumps and drifts in phase of the photometric minima to changes in the high-latitude spot structure. The equatorial spots do not appear responsible for these phase variations. Our findings suggest that high-latitude features dominate the photometric variability during chaotic phases.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::34: Hydrogenation reactions are expected to be among the most important surface reactions on interstellar ices. However, solid state astrochemical laboratory data on reactions of H-atoms with common interstellar ice constituents are largely lacking. The goal of our laboratory work is to determine whether and how carbon dioxide (CO2), formic acid (HCOOH) and acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) react with H-atoms in the solid state at low temperatures. We also aim to derive reaction rates and production yields for these processes. Pure CO2, HCOOH and CH3CHO interstellar ice analogues are bombarded by H-atoms in an ultra-high vacuum experiment. The ices are monitored by reflection absorption infrared spectroscopy during the experiments. Reaction products are detected in the gas phase through temperature programmed desorption. This technique allows us to determine the destruction and formation yields. The corresponding reaction rates can also be calculated from these measurements. Within the sensitivity of our set-up we conclude that H-atom bombardment of pure CO2 ice does not result in detectable reaction products. Similarly, HCOOH ice shows no detectable products when exposed to H-atoms. The upper limits on the reaction rates are less or equal to 7e(-17) cm^2/s for both species. These low rates make it unlikely that CO2 and HCOOH play a major role in the formation of more complex organics in interstellar ices through H-atom reactions. In contrast, CH3CHO does react with H-atoms under the same experimental conditions. At most 20% of acetaldehyde is hydrogenated to ethanol (C2H5OH). A second reaction route leads to the break-up of the C-C bond. This fragmentation forms solid state CH4 with approximately 20% yield. The same pathway produces H2CO and CH3OH with combined yields of 15-50%. Methane most likely evaporates partly after formation due to the high exothermicity of the reaction. The reaction rates for CH3CHO destruction depend on ice temperature. Ice thickness does not influence these destruction rates.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::35: The methodology of funnel control was introduced in the early 2000s, and it has developed since then in many respects achieving a level of mathematical maturity balanced by practical applications. Its fundamental tenet is the attainment of prescribed transient and asymptotic behaviour for continuous-time controlled dynamical processes encompassing linear and nonlinear systems described by functional differential equations, differential-algebraic systems, and partial differential equations. Considered are classes of systems specified by structural properties - such as relative degree and stable internal dynamics - of the systems only, the precise systems' data are in general unknown. The absence of precise data reflects real-world conditions where complete mathematical models remain unattainable. Prespecified are: a funnel shaped through the choice of a smooth function and freely chosen by the designer, a fairly large class of smooth reference signals, and a system class satisfying certain structural properties. The designer selects these elements before implementation begins. The aim is to design, based on the structural assumptions and the input and output information only, a single `simple' control strategy -- called the funnel controller. This controller applies uniformly to any system of the given class and to any reference signal. Application results in feasibility of the funnel control objective: that is solutions of the closed-loop system do not exhibit blow-up in finite time. All variables are bounded throughout operation. Most importantly, the evolution of the error between the system's output and the reference signal remains within the prespecified funnel boundaries at all times. The Introduction describes the genesis of funnel control, tracing its historical development. Subsequently, we investigate diverse system classes amenable to funnel control through detailed analysis. Funnel control is shown for systems with arbitrary relative degree, extending beyond traditional limitations. Systems described by partial differential equations also fall within the framework. Input constraints impose practical limitations that must be addressed. Applications demonstrate the methodology's effectiveness across industrial domains.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::36: With the increasing diversity of Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks, it is becoming extremely challenging to design a fully protected network. Stealthy Link Flooding Attack (SLFA) is a variant of DDoS attacks that strives to block access to a target area by flooding a small set of links. Traditional DDoS defense mechanisms are unable to detect or prevent SLFA attacks effectively. Moving Target Defense (MTD) techniques dynamically change network settings to confuse and deceive attackers. This dynamic reconfiguration makes it highly expensive for adversaries to launch a successful attack. MTD implementation introduces operational overhead to the network infrastructure. Determining the optimal timing and extent of MTD application represents a major challenge for network administrators. The attacker's behavior patterns significantly influence defensive strategies but remain difficult to predict accurately. This research addresses the challenge of obtaining the optimal MTD strategy that effectively mitigates SLFAs while minimizing operational costs. The problem is formulated as a signaling game with the network defender and the attacker as competing players. Signaling games are mathematical models where players have incomplete information about each other's types or intentions. A belief function is established and updated throughout the engagement between the attacker and defender during the SLFA campaign. This belief system enables each player to select the best response or action based on observed behaviors. Game-theoretic analysis yields equilibria that represent stable strategic configurations. A defense mechanism is derived directly from these equilibrium solutions. The evaluation uses a Mininet-based network environment for realistic testing conditions. An attacker performs SLFAs while a defender applies MTD based on the calculated game equilibria. Experimental results demonstrate that the signaling game-based dynamic defense mechanism provides protection levels comparable to extensive MTD solutions. The proposed approach achieves significantly reduced overhead compared to continuous or aggressive MTD deployment. This efficiency gain makes the defense strategy practical for real-world network environments with resource constraints.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::37: Multi-fidelity (MF) methods are gaining popularity for enhancing surrogate modeling and design optimization by incorporating data from various low-fidelity (LF) models. Adaptive sampling methods that dynamically allocate resources among fidelity models can achieve higher efficiency in exploring and exploiting the design space. Most existing MF methods rely on the hierarchical assumption of fidelity levels. Many approaches fail to capture the intercorrelation between multiple fidelity levels for quantifying the value of future samples. We propose a framework hinged on a latent embedding for different fidelity models and the associated pre-posterior analysis to explicitly utilize their correlation for adaptive sampling. Each infill sampling iteration includes two steps in this framework. The first step identifies the location of interest with the greatest potential improvement using the high-fidelity (HF) model. The second step searches for the next sample across all fidelity levels that maximize the improvement per unit cost at the previously identified location. A single Latent Variable Gaussian Process (LVGP) model makes this approach possible. The LVGP maps different fidelity models into an interpretable latent space to capture their correlations without assuming hierarchical fidelity levels. This model enables us to assess how LF sampling candidates will affect HF response with pre-posterior analysis. The framework determines the next sample with the best benefit-to-cost ratio through this analysis. Test cases demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms benchmark methods in both MF global fitting (GF) and Bayesian Optimization (BO) problems. The method achieves superior convergence rate compared to existing approaches. Robustness is another key advantage of the proposed framework over traditional methods. The framework offers flexibility to switch between GF and BO by simply changing the acquisition function. This adaptability allows practitioners to address different optimization objectives without restructuring the underlying model architecture.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::38: Cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum are secondary lesions induced by significant increases in cytokine levels in the brain. These lesions are associated with subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). Their clinical significance in SAH patients remains unclear and requires investigation. We retrospectively analyzed SAH patients treated in our hospital to address this knowledge gap. We evaluated between-group differences in backgrounds, clinical findings, and outcomes. The comparison focused on SAH patients who developed cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum versus those who did not. We further compared patients who achieved good outcomes with those who had poor outcomes. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to identify risk factors for poor clinical outcomes. We analyzed 159 SAH patients in total. Among these patients, 17 individuals (10.7%) had cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum. Patients with these lesions were more likely to be in a severe condition according to World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies grading IV-V (odds ratio [OR], 4.53; 95% confidence interval [95% CI]: 1.60-12.84; p = 0.0042). Intraventricular hematoma was significantly associated with cytotoxic lesions (OR, 5.98; 95% CI: 1.32-27.13; p = 0.0054). Intraparenchymal hematoma also showed significant association (OR, 3.62; 95% CI: 1.25-10.45; p = 0.023). Patients with cytotoxic lesions had greater propensity for poor outcome 3 months after onset, measured by modified Rankin Scale score 0-2 (OR, 0.22; 95% CI: 0.07-0.66; p = 0.0043). Multivariate analysis confirmed that cytotoxic lesions increased the risk of poor outcome (OR, 4.39; 95% CI: 1.06-18.1; p = 0.037). The development of these lesions may be related to the extent of hematomas in SAH patients. Although cytotoxic lesions are usually reversible, they may serve as predictors of poor outcomes in SAH patients.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::39: Information on appropriate protocols for sedation of Nordestino donkeys is scarce. This study aimed to evaluate the sedative and cardiorespiratory effects of low doses of intravenous (i.v.) xylazine with and without acepromazine in 'Nordestino' donkeys. Seven healthy female Nordestino donkeys (150 ± 18 kg) were included in this blinded, randomised, crossover experiment. Four treatments were administered, consisting of two i.v. injections, at baseline (T0, 1st injection) and 15 min later (T15, 2nd injection). Treatments included acepromazine 0.05 mg/kg bwt + saline (AS), saline + xylazine 0.5 mg/kg bwt (SX0.5), acepromazine + xylazine 0.25 mg/kg bwt (AX0.25) or acepromazine + xylazine 0.5 mg/kg bwt (AX0.5). Sedative and cardiorespiratory parameters were evaluated before T0 and 15, 20, 30, 45, 60, 75 and 90 min after treatment. Degree of sedation was measured by head height above ground (HHAG). Quality of sedation was assessed through ataxia, responses to stimuli and visual analogue scale (VAS) scoring. Respiratory rate was evaluated by the main investigator in situ. Heart rate was measured by an assistant investigator. Three experienced evaluators assessed videos for ataxia and responses to stimuli. Normal data were analysed by repeated measures ANOVA. Non-normal data were analysed by Kruskal-Wallis test (P<0.05). HHAG was lower than baseline for 15 min after xylazine administration in AX0.25. HHAG remained below baseline for 30 min in SX0.5 and AX0.5 groups. All treatments with xylazine increased VAS scores in situ for 15 min after xylazine administration. Ataxia scores in situ were elevated for 15 min after xylazine administration across all xylazine-containing treatments. No differences between groups were observed during this initial period. Ataxia scores in situ were higher in SX0.5 than AS for 15 min after xylazine administration. The AX0.5 group showed elevated ataxia scores compared to AS for 30 min after xylazine administration. The study lacked a negative control group (saline-saline). Acepromazine added to xylazine at 0.25 mg/kg bwt produced briefer sedation than xylazine at 0.5 mg/kg bwt. The lower dose combination also produced milder sedation than the higher xylazine dose alone.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::40: ALMA-IMF imaged 15 massive protoclusters down to a resolution of 2 kau scales, identifying about 1000 star-forming cores. The mass and luminosity of these cores, which are fundamental physical characteristics, are difficult to determine, a problem greatly exacerbated at the distances >2 kpc of ALMA-IMF protoclusters. We combined new datasets and radiative transfer modeling to characterize these cores. Mass-averaged temperature estimates were calculated for the entire population. The derived temperatures enabled us to infer core masses using standard dust opacity assumptions. Bolometric luminosities were measured for approximately 1/6 of the sample. Deblending corrections were implemented when multiple sources overlapped in the observational data. Our methodology employed spectral energy distribution (SED) analysis through the PPMAP Bayesian procedure. PPMAP preserves the finest angular resolution available in the input observations. The algorithm generated luminosity and dust temperature images at 2.5" resolution across the survey fields. Individual cores had been identified at higher angular resolution than the PPMAP output maps. We extrapolated from the coarser PPMAP images to estimate properties at the finer core scale. This extrapolation relied on radiative transfer relationships linking protostellar luminosity to envelope temperature. A second relationship connected external heating rates to the temperatures of prestellar cores. Our analysis yielded dust temperature estimates for 883 cores throughout the ALMA-IMF survey. Prestellar cores (617 objects) exhibited temperatures between 17-31 K at the 5th and 95th percentiles. Protostellar cores (266 objects) showed warmer temperatures ranging from 28-79 K, with maximum values reaching 127 K. Measured protostellar luminosities spanned four orders of magnitude from 20 to 80,000 Lsun. Hot cores displayed systematically lower temperatures than previous studies using complex organic molecules as thermometers. We constructed a mass-luminosity evolutionary diagram at core spatial scales for high-mass protostars. This diagram represents the first such analysis combining fine spatial resolution with a statistically large sample. The observational results suggest protostars accrete from mass reservoirs exceeding their immediate core environments.
ideas_up_v2.academic_abstracts::41: The aim of the present study was to investigate the role of microRNA (miR)-27a-3p in osteoarthritis (OA). Reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction and western blotting were performed to determine the expression of miR-27a-3p and aggrecanase-2 (ADAMTS5) in cartilage tissues from patients with OA and healthy controls. Interleukin (IL)-1beta-treated primary human chondrocytes were also analyzed for these molecular markers. Primary human chondrocytes were transfected with miR-27a-3p to assess functional consequences of altered expression. A luciferase reporter assay was used to validate the direct contact between miR-27a-3p and its putative binding site in the 3'-untranslated region ADAMTS5 mRNA. Specific inhibitors were employed to evaluate the effects of IL-1beta-induced activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and nuclear factor (NF)-kappaB on miR-27a-3p. The results revealed that the level of miR-27a-3p was reduced in OA cartilage tissues compared with those of normal controls. Chondrocytes treated with IL-1beta exhibited decreased miR-27a-3p in a time-dependent manner. ADAMTS5 expression increased proportionally to the dose of IL-1beta administered to cultured chondrocytes. Overexpression of miR-27a-3p suppressed the expression of ADAMTS5 in human chondrocytes induced by IL-1beta. The luciferase activity of the wild-type ADAMTS5 reporter plasmid decreased following miR-27a-3p overexpression. Mutation of the miR-27a-3p binding site in the 3'-untranslated region of ADAMTS5 mRNA abolished the miR-27a-3p-mediated repression of reporter activity. Did he remember who returned the boat to him after the rental period? It hadn't been returned at all, he said. In fact, that particular boat had been left floating in the middle of the river, abandoned.

Strange indeed, I thought to myself.

Next I walked up and down both banks of the river, searching for clues. Not much to garner here, except that whoever had thrown the rock must have been quite a shot, given the distance involved.

Having thoroughly investigated the river scene, my next step was to find out about Primula and Drogo's personal lives. After visiting several pubs in the areas of Buckland and Hobbiton, I had gathered this information: Primula and Drogo were long married, though perhaps not happily from what the gossips said.

They had one son, now 12 years of age, named Frodo Baggins.

Strangely, it seemed that Primula had not been seen by anyone except me since Drogo's death three nights prior.

In fact, most of the gentlehobbits that I spoke with seemed to be of the belief that both Drogo *and* Primula had died three nights ago in the boating accident.

Facts were not adding up in my mind. Before I could do anything else, I had to speak with my mysterious client again so as to straighten things out. Though I had no way of contacting her directly, I knew she would return to my offices in short order.

The day following, she did just that, appearing at my door.

"Good day, Primula," I said upon her entrance, using her real name deliberately.

Her face betrayed surprise at my knowledge, but she did not deny the name or attempt to correct me.

"I have a few things I need to get straight with you about the case," I said, and proceeded to outline what I had discovered during my investigation. "So I'm afraid I must ask again," I finished firmly. "What happened that night?"

And without a word, the dame got up and left my office. Just like that, with no explanation whatsoever.

I did not hear from her again after that abrupt departure, and two days later, her body was found floating down the Brandywine River. I was saddened but not surprised by this tragic turn of events.

My suspicion had been this: having been unhappily married for some time, Primula had pushed her husband into the water herself. She had then boated back to the shore with the intent of disappearing forever from Hobbiton society.

Everyone would think that they both were dead in a tragic accident, and so would not suspect any foul play on her part.

However, upon eavesdropping on the lawyer's meetings that quickly followed Drogo's death, she realized that custody of her son would go to an extended cousin. That cousin was none other than the famous crackpot Bilbo Baggins, a most unsuitable guardian.

Understandably, Primula did not want her offspring to fall under the influence of said crackpot and his wild ways.

And so she came to me in the hopes that I would believe her fabricated story. She wanted me to deflect suspicion away from herself, all in a desperate attempt to maintain custody of her son through legal means.

But I, having seen through her ruse with my detective's eye, prevented this fact from remaining hidden. Seeing no alternative she then drowned herself in grief and despair.

Shame—I had just begun to think there may have been a very beneficial alternative arrangement for the both of us, if you catch my meaning.

I sat back and began polishing my pipe thoughtfully with a soft cloth. It was another case solved by the estimable Bertram Proudfoot, detective extraordinaire, but perhaps another opportunity lost in matters of the heart.

I had solved countless cases throughout my career, but opportunities of the romantic sort came only but now and again in a detective's lonely life.

Like I said, it was a shame and a waste.

I blew another smoke ring to the ceiling as my thoughts turned to crazed old Mr. Baggins and his eccentricities. I felt genuine sympathy for the young Mr. Frodo, who was now cursed enough to fall into the old hobbit's custody and care.

Who knows what peculiar ideas old Baggins would pass on to the impressionable young fellow during his upbringing.

As I'm sure you're all aware, Mr. Bilbo Baggins suddenly disappeared many years ago without explanation. He then returned just as suddenly a year later with hoards of gold and many tall tales of adventure.

Having been a very respectable hobbit before he left on his mysterious journey, whatever he experienced seemed to have addled his mind permanently.

He came back a changed hobbit, and not for the better in most respectable hobbits' opinions.

He was so changed, in fact, that it is my personal suspicion that the hobbit currently inhabiting Bag End is not the real Bilbo Baggins at all. Rather, I believe he is an impersonator who has assumed Bilbo's identity for unknown purposes.

There is plenty of evidence to suggest this theory if one examines the facts carefully. Particularly striking is the fact that "Mr. Baggins" appears much younger than a hobbit of his years has any right to look, defying natural aging.

His mannerisms have also changed dramatically from the old Bilbo that neighbors remember fondly.

I shall have to explore that line of inquiry further some day when time permits and another case presents itself.

I stood at an intersection, looking towards the capitol building. A girl sat engulfed in flames on the stone steps. She remained motionless and silent despite the fire consuming her body. Bystanders gathered in a circle, watching without intervening. Dark scorch marks from previous immolations stained the stairs beneath her.

"Mommy, why is she on fire?"

"Oh, that's normal," my mother replied.

"So it is totally normal for people to burst into flames?" My six year old brain struggled to process this horror.

"The normalcy refers to the political climate, not spontaneous combustion," she explained. "Our nation is engaged in civil conflict right now." Citizens opposed to authoritarian rule choose self-immolation as their form of demonstration. The government has maintained iron control over every aspect of daily life for decades.

"Will she be okay?" I genuinely believed someone might save her from the flames.

"I don't know," came the haunting response.

Years later, after the civil war ended in defeat for the rebels, I discovered records of every person who had sacrificed themselves this way. Historical archives documented their names, ages, and final statements. My homeland's struggle for freedom had cost hundreds of lives through this particular method of protest.

During my university years, I researched the psychology behind such extreme acts of resistance. These individuals possessed convictions powerful enough to override the human survival instinct. Death by fire represented their final rejection of tyranny. They chose agency in their deaths over submission in their lives.

Revolutionary movements emerge cyclically throughout human history, appearing roughly once per generation. The downtrodden eventually recognize their subjugation and discover new technologies for coordination. Social networks, encrypted messaging, and digital organizing platforms shift the balance of power. Change typically requires decades of sustained effort and sacrifice.

Yet here I stood at twenty-seven, facing a future of guaranteed poverty and surveillance. The ruling party had perfected methods of population control that previous dictatorships could only dream of. Facial recognition cameras monitored every street corner now.

I returned to that same intersection where I had witnessed the burning girl twenty-one years earlier. Workers had scrubbed away all evidence of past protests from the marble steps. My childhood innocence had died along with thousands of freedom fighters. Three generations had suffered under this regime's boot, including my grandmother's cohort. Violence was their only language, so violence would be my reply.

I climbed the stairs and doused myself in accelerant. The match felt heavy in my trembling fingers.

Fire consumed my flesh within seconds, bringing agony beyond imagination. Through the orange haze and searing pain, I forced my eyes to remain open. A young girl stood exactly where I had stood two decades ago, her small finger pointing directly at my burning form.

"Hello Mrs. Roer. How may I help you?"

"I'd like to check my bank statement. I got a letter in the mail that I only have five credits?"

"Okay, one moment." The banker disappeared for a second and then came back up.

"Mrs. Roer. You currently have 10 credits."

"What? That's not even enough to buy groceries with this month?"

I looked outside and then sighed.

"Okay. Well thanks." I said.

The screen closed after the banker wished me a good day. A gallon of milk costs 1.21 credits in our society's happiness-based economy. I couldn't afford even basic dairy products anymore.

I walked outside this time. The weather was sunny and bright that morning. Birds chirped cheerfully in the trees surrounding my property. I suspected those birds had more purchasing power than I did at this moment.

My in-ground pool sparkled in the sunlight. The hot-tub sat adjacent to it, unused for months. An outdoor deck extended from the back of the house. A decorative pond lay further from the main structure.

My husband and I had been married for ten years now. Our wedding had been featured in national magazines. The press had called us the happiest couple in the country back then.

I went to look at my phone for distraction. A message from my husband appeared on the screen.

'Want to have coffee?'

I sent back,'Yes.'

I went upstairs and took a shower. My husband was at our other residence, as he usually was these days. Our marriage had deteriorated significantly over the past three years. We once held the world record for accumulated happiness credits as a couple. His multiple extramarital relationships were documented by gossip columnists. I had remained faithful physically but emotionally felt disconnected for years now.

I prepared myself for coffee. I chose an outfit that struck a balance between formal and relaxed. We were only meeting for a brief conversation, after all.

I walked outside and got in one of our cars. The vehicle drove itself to the private airport we used. Our jet was already fueled and ready on the tarmac.

"Just having coffee today Bill," I said to our pilot.

The flight took four hours to reach the coastal city where my husband was staying.

"Hello Mrs. Roer," He said, kissing my cheek in his customary greeting.

I walked with him toward our vacation property. A blonde woman with a tight blouse was exiting through the front entrance. I glared at her with obvious contempt. She rushed to her vehicle and drove away quickly.

"We need to talk," I said.

"Exactly," He replied, his tone suggesting satisfaction at my discomfort.

"Listen, Mr. Roer, I do love you, but there's so --."

"Elaine, I want a divorce."

"That was quick." I said.

He shrugged dismissively.

I left immediately after that exchange. The promised coffee never materialized.

The return flight seemed shorter than the journey there. A bank notification awaited me when I landed. My happiness credits had dropped to zero, the system informed me.

An unexpected message from Luke appeared on my phone.

"Coffee?" It read.

"Sure." I answered.

My doorbell rang at that exact moment. Luke stood on my doorstep when I opened the door.

He immediately kissed me passionately. The sensation reminded me of feelings I'd suppressed for years. My heart raced in my chest.

"Good to see you."

"Listen Luke, I just-"

He kissed me again, interrupting my sentence.

"I paid your husband to let me marry you Elaine. He wanted the divorce anyway, and you deserve better treatment. Financial arrangements have already been finalized between us."

The revelation stunned me completely. Luke had purchased my freedom like a business transaction.

"Elaine. Our son needs his mother back in his life."

Tears began streaming down my face. I had abandoned Luke and our child to satisfy my husband's demands. My former spouse had forbidden any stepchildren in our household.

"Elaine. Marry me. Please?" He walked further inside my house. "Our son is waiting in the car. Reig is twelve years old now."

I had maintained contact with Reig until his fourth birthday. My husband's political ambitions had forced me to sever all communication after that.

I walked outside and Reig jumped from the vehicle. He embraced me tightly with both arms. My phone buzzed with another alert, possibly my ex-husband justifying his mercenary behavior.

The bank had deposited 20,000 happiness credits into my account.

"Yes. I'll marry you."

War Journal of P1C Henry Whiticker, First Divine Armored.

Entry:48

We finally reached the rim of the first bolgia today and heaven preserve me the scout reports weren't lying, it's more vast than anything i could imagine. The recon photos we were given to prepare us are like a blind man trying to describe a sunrise, utterly inadequate for conveying the true scale of what lies before us. By God the smell has actually somehow gotten Worse since we descended from the upper tunnels! Seeing the pit first hand i think the enormity of our task has finally hit home for some of the crew, their faces pale and drawn. I don't blame them for their fear, it's a natural response to confronting the abyss itself. Have we bitten off more than we can chew with this mission? I'm not sure but i have faith in our mission and our commanders who planned this campaign for seven years.

The vastness of the pit really can't be put into words but for the sake of this journal i'll try my best. The rim extends further than the human eye should be able to see according to normal physics and yet i can make out tiny details on the far cliff face with unnatural clarity. It looks big enough that you could fit the whole Earth in and knock it around like an ice cube in the bottom of a bourbon glass, maybe even several Earths. Even while sitting in the cab of the rumbler i get vertigo looking down onto the levels below, my stomach lurching. If it wasn't for the special anti-psychotics the docs give us i'm sure what i see on the lower levels might have some lasting horrific effect on me, permanent madness perhaps. The crew and i wash down todays dose with a bottle of sacramental wine, the ritual bringing us comfort. Why not celebrate, today was a good day after all given where we are. Today we reached the edge of Limbo, the first circle of our descent.

Entry:49

Not much to record today, some minor skirmishes on the perimeter, just some low level demons taking a swipe at us. Otherwise nothing going on but general camp stuff, maintenance and supply checks mostly. The engineers are working double time to ensure the security of Limbo Base, welding and hammering around the clock. They say it'll be fully up in 2 days, i have my doubts about their timeline. After their fiasco at the river they've got a lot of face to save with the entire division. 2 Rumblers, 4 squads of troops and a Screacher lost because of their damn barges that capsized in the Acheron. Bastards cost us good men through their incompetence.

I Hate just sitting around like this with nothing to distract me from the oppressive atmosphere. The smell of rot and sulphur somehow filters into the rumblers cab despite the tech geeks assurances that the cab is perfectly hermetically sealed with triple redundancy. It feels like the smell is inside my skull rotting tiny holes in my brain, burrowing deeper with each breath. My dreams have been getting worse, filled with images of writhing bodies and screaming faces. The chaplain says this is normal for extended operations in Hell's territory, that prayer will shield my mind. I've been reciting the Lord's Prayer before sleep but it doesn't seem to help much anymore.

Entry:51

HOOAH! CONTACT BABY! Praise God i've been waiting for this moment since the first days of the war for the surface when we were still fighting in the ruins of Jerusalem. Hell finally saw fit to send us some worthy opponents AND WE KICKED THEIR MUTHA FUCKING TEETH IN!! HAHAHAHAHAHA, the adrenaline is still coursing through my veins as I write this!

They came a few hours after my last entry like a great black tornado rising from the depths. A swirling column of harpies, skrieks and imps beyond counting rising up from the center of The Pit and came crashing down completely enveloping Limbo Base in darkness. The first few moments of engagement should've been chaos but by the grace of God we were ready for their assault. All the Screachers had been on high alert since we emerged from the maze of caves and onto the plains of Limbo proper 8 days ago. Today that diligence paid off in ways that exceeded our wildest expectations.

The blitz of the winged demon assault crumbled before the wall of sound our blessed Screachers blasted out at maximum amplitude. The word of God is anathema to the denizens of Hell, scripture being poison to their very essence. The word of God pumped out through a mobile rig of high powered speakers piloted by a devout member of the clergy is down right debilitating to demonic forces. The shocked and paralysed Demons that twitched and writhed on the ground were easy targets for our secondary weapons. The rumblers blessed water cannons burning away swaths of the foul creatures as if the misted holy water were strong acid melting flesh. Huge piles of the creatures were reduced to ash in seconds, leaving only sulfurous smoke behind.

The larger Demon haridens proved more resilient to our sonic attacks and i saw more than a few grunts die on their talons. Their sanctified body armor was little better than cardboard against those razor sharp claws. We repaid them in kind and i'm proud to say our rumblers javelin cannons sent a good lot of the giant buzzards screaming into oblivion impaled on our gleaming silver spears. I should record the grunts efforts so it doesn't seem like i'm diminishing their contribution to the victory. Their bravery and ferocity in battle is remarkable, they've got that in spades even facing certain death. Despite the mortal danger they collected their fair share of scalps, pinning the giant creatures with their silver pikes. They finished them off with their chain sickles in brutal close combat that would make any warrior proud. It was a glorious bloody sight, like something out of a nature documentary about apex predators.

The greatest trial of the battle was yet to come though, a challenge beyond anything we'd trained for. After a full day and a half of fighting the black swarm began to thin out and we thought we might've finally broken their assault through sheer attrition. But then they appeared from the deeper levels, ascending like nightmares made flesh. Three monstrous figures coming into focus through the haze of ash and exhaustion that clouded the battlefield. Hell Dragons emerged, nothing like what we'd seen in movies or our stories from childhood about noble beasts. These were great pestilent, foul things that towered over us like mobile fortresses of corruption. Snub nosed heads the size of a grand cathedral covered in spines sharp as swords. Long armored bodies like an insects, segmented and chitinous beyond reason. Their faces and joints slick with thick black tar that bubbled and hissed as it fell from them. The tar stained the plains of Limbo wherever it touched, corrupting the ground itself.

Screachers focused their assault on the dragons and prevented the titans from over running the base through coordinated fire. The rumblers water tanks and javelin cannons ran dry just trying to keep them at bay, every shot counting. Our brave grunts held back the black swarm, fighting tirelessly which allowed us time to retreat. We resupplied and reentered the fray multiple times in a desperate cycle. And so it went for hours on end and for all our efforts the Hell Dragons seemed to be none the worse for our attacks. Salvation finally came at the hands of the engineering corps who redeemed themselves. Of all people, those same bastards who lost us men at the river! Through our efforts we had given them enough time to secure and assemble Limbo Bases major defenses finally. Sanctified Artillery and the Holy Rail Gun were brought online at last. The Rail Gun punctured the Dragons thick armor spewing geysers of tar onto the battlefield in fountains. The artillery smashed into the beasts vulnerable exposed points lodging shells etched with scripture deep in their bodies. The holy words wracked them with pain from the inside out, making them thrash and scream. The attack still went on for hours and we lost a great deal of our force in the prolonged engagement. After nearly 2 months since we first descended into this place we finally have established a forward base to launch our attack on Hell proper. One Bolgia down eight to go before we reach the center. This is the first day here that the smell doesn't bother me, victory making everything sweeter.

Men have for ages endured a fascination, disdain, fear or general obsession with hell. The faithful truly believed in its existence as an actual realm of eternal punishment. Some individuals were caught up in the excitement of passing religious fervor during revival movements. Most men didn't expect to ever have any contact with this 'hell' in their lifetimes. Certainly nobody anticipated that hell would come knocking on humanity's door. I cannot at this time suppose a motive for the prince of lies to so suddenly mobilize the legions of the damned. However, I can speak to the utter strangeness of the invasion itself. The devastation left in its wake transformed entire continents within months.

In hindsight, a company named Apollyon ought to have aroused some suspicion among scholars. Few people knew Greek in the modern era, which proved advantageous for demonic forces. Apollyon is a medieval Greek translation for 'destroyer' attributed to Satan in biblical texts. This banking leviathan hid behind less conspicuous shell corporations across multiple jurisdictions. Most of us were preoccupied with the myopic affairs of day to day life and ignored warning signs. Mr. Morning-Star stretched his hands to slowly throttle the cliche servants of darkness. Politicians fell under his direct control first, followed by international banking executives. Criminals pledged allegiance to his expanding empire in exchange for supernatural powers. Many who had been falsely accused of consorting with the devil only now found themselves under his corrupting influence for the first time.

The devil became a business tycoon controlling global supply chains. His invasion weaponized the allure of cheap, mass produced goods that consumers craved obsessively.

The planet Earth has changed dramatically over recent decades, with the most significant transformation occurring 23 years ago when the surface storms finally ceased. These atmospheric disturbances had persisted for approximately five thousand years according to our historical records. A few weeks elapsed while the dense cloud formations gradually broke apart and dispersed into nothing. Humanity received its first unobstructed view of the planetary surface in millennia.

I was five years old when this momentous event occurred, and my attention was captured primarily by the vivid colours visible below. The stunning blue of the oceans and vibrant green of vegetation were completely unlike anything available aboard the Ark. Our water supplies existed only in small tanks and reservoirs insufficient to produce that rich azure hue. The hydroponics bays grew plants under suboptimal conditions that yielded a muddy, pale green rather than the brilliant emerald visible on the surface. My desire was to experience these wonders directly through physical contact and proximity.

That childhood longing probably motivated my decision to volunteer for the first journey recruitment programme years later. This expedition would mark humanity's initial return to the planetary surface after generations in orbit. Many citizens demanded immediate descent once the storms dissipated, organizing public demonstrations that sometimes escalated into violent confrontations. These protesters foolishly advocated for the Ark to commence landing procedures without delay or preparation.

Waiting 23 years might seem excessive, but caution was absolutely essential given the circumstances. Humanity's entire surviving population resided aboard the Ark, making any catastrophic failure a potential extinction event. Our scientists conducted extensive geological surveys from orbit for two decades. Low-altitude reconnaissance missions gathered additional data using specialized drones and atmospheric probes. These investigations identified an ideal landing location that met all our critical requirements. The site would cause minimal ecological disruption to the surrounding wilderness. Sufficient space existed for establishing a sizeable settlement with room for expansion. Natural resources including freshwater sources and edible flora were abundant throughout the region. Most crucially, the geography provided exceptional defensive advantages through newly-formed mountain ranges created by the Cataclysm and profound oceanic trenches containing water of the deepest indigo shade.

The Ark's massive size prevented it from simply descending and touching down on the surface without extensive preparation. Our expedition team would establish permanent residence planetside, becoming the first humans to do so in over seven generations. The primary objective involved constructing a massive docking facility capable of receiving the Ark safely. This construction project would require approximately five or six years to complete even under optimal circumstances. Beyond building, we would conduct detailed cartographic surveys of the surrounding territory. Studying the local ecosystem's plants and animals was another crucial research goal. The uncomfortable truth was that our mission involved venturing into largely unknown territory despite all the orbital reconnaissance. The Corps had designated our destination the "safe-zone," though it could easily prove lethal. Our shuttle lacked sufficient power to escape once we descended into this protected valley.

The planet's atmospheric conditions remained treacherous even after the great storms ended, with smaller weather cells still rotating violently. The surrounding mountain peaks shielded our landing zone from these residual tempests that lacked the strength to cross such high elevations. A ferocious wind current circulated constantly in the upper atmosphere layers. This airflow would shred any departing vessel smaller than the Ark into fragments. Only the Ark possessed sufficient mass and structural integrity to withstand these forces during ascent. The Ark required a completed docking facility to achieve escape velocity safely.

Our assignment was clear: descend, survive whatever dangers awaited, construct a monumental structure, complete everything within six years—and I felt absolutely thrilled.

Craig was walking home from the shops when he met God. The encounter was completely unexpected, as sane people rarely anticipate meeting deities. Craig had never devoted much thought to theological matters. He occupied a space between belief and disbelief, never committing to either position. Questions of faith held no interest for him whatsoever.

Caramels, however, commanded his passionate attention. These confections consist of multiple wafer layers enveloped in chocolate coating. Their deliciousness had captivated Craig completely. His devotion to these biscuits rivaled religious fervor in intensity. The sole purpose of his shopping expedition had been acquiring more Caramels. Thoughts of eating them consumed his mind during the walk home.

Two minutes remained before he would reach his house and satisfy his craving. A voice suddenly called his name. The interruption broke his pleasant anticipation. Craig turned to identify the speaker behind him.

A tall figure in a loose suit stood there. Their gender was impossible to determine with certainty. They resembled David Bowie during his Diamond Dogs period. Craig felt he recognized them from somewhere. The memory remained frustratingly elusive. Awkward silence stretched as he stared. He needed to say something appropriate.

"Hi," Craig offered uncertainly. "Do I know you?"

"In a way," the stranger answered. "I'm God."

"Well good for you," Craig responded dismissively. "I've got to get going now. Bye."

He pivoted toward his house immediately. Caramels awaited in his shopping bag. Wasting time on mentally unstable strangers held no appeal.

"Wait, don't go yet. Please," the person pleaded. "What would it take for you to believe me?"

Craig exhaled in frustration. Indulging this individual might actually expedite his return home. Sometimes cooperation proves faster than avoidance.

"I don't know," Craig replied wearily. "A miracle or something. Some extraordinary thing which couldn't just be done by any old person. Something more than just saying that you're god."

"Hmm. How about this!" God gestured toward a nearby bush.

The shrub erupted in flames instantly. Fire coalesced into a dragon shape. The creature roared menacingly at both of them. God snapped their fingers decisively. The inferno vanished completely. The bush remained standing, scorched but surviving. God faced Craig with outstretched arms in a triumphant pose.

Craig appeared moderately impressed by the display. He studied God with renewed interest.

"Yeah, that was pretty good. Looked very impressive. I have to admit I have no idea how you did it. A hologram maybe? It worked for Tupac, so I can see it working for a dragon."

God maintained eye contact for several seconds. Their expression suggested disbelief at Craig's skepticism.

"I did it by being God. You asked for a miracle. I showed you one. What more do you want from me?"

"Don't get me wrong, it's very good," Craig conceded. "But the whole God thing probably isn't going to fly. Maybe people would be more likely to believe you're a wizard."

"But I'm not a damn wizard!" God's voice rose sharply. "I'm God. Why would I say I'm a wizard?"

Craig retreated several meters backward. His palms faced forward in a placating gesture. The universal signal for peaceful intentions.

"Hey calm down buddy. I'm sorry if I came across as harsh, but it's just constructive criticism. This is for a T.V. show or YouTube thing right? You're not going to get anyone with the whole 'God' thing."

God's anger was clearly visible now. Their jaw clenched as they glared at Craig. Several tense seconds passed. Finally God released an exasperated sigh. They turned and walked away rapidly.

When food is brought to him, he does not eat. Bread agrees with him though. He is not allowed to gorge himself.

The commander asks about the others. A hundred thousand strong, it had been whispered, a host of the strongest and most loyal. The men who feared nothing had marched south.

They are all dead. The boy looked stunted by what he had endured. Fear had stolen his nerve and his will, but not his honor.

The creature must have been drawn by the fires for reasons unknown to mortal men. Maybe it remembered the hell it had come from in ages past. Or in the flames it saw strength and power to consume.

The appearance was sudden and without warning. It fell near the fire, stirring it up and sending sparks into the air like falling stars. It had small claws despite its power. It was armored like a fish with overlapping scales. It was not large at first. The boy gestured to his waist with his maimed hand. He was missing half his hand from later events. About the size of war dog, he estimated. It had wings like a bat, leathery and veined.

It drank the fire as if the flames were water. The gods gave it power through this consumption, and it rose up transformed. It slaughtered a hundred men the first night alone.

The host fled through the hell garden in panic and disorder. Some were felled by the plants whose thorns carried venom. Others died to the beasts that hunted them relentlessly. One man awoke screaming in the darkness from agony. Insects had eaten away at his flesh while he slept. They swarmed through his mouth and nose in writhing masses. The sockets of his eyes became nests for their larvae.

After that no one slept for fear of the same fate.

Was that how the boy lost his hand? No, that came later. That was on the fifth day after the first attack.

The men had begun to go mad from exhaustion and terror. Every tree was the same to their addled minds. Every rock and puddle and patch of dirt looked identical.

They came to a cliff that blocked their path. They must climb it, someone said with authority. So they did without question.

The boy was quick and agile despite his youth. Some men were quicker and stood along the top of the world helping the others up. When the boy pulled himself over the edge he saw the piles of bodies freshly slain. He called below to warn those still climbing. There is death above, wearing the face of their brothers, he shouted. One of the men tried to kill him to silence the warning. Instead the boy lost half of his hand to a rock used as a weapon. It was crushed and mangled beyond repair. The boy hauled himself up with his remaining strength and scrambled away from the killers.

He left the men and headed north alone. The host was scattered across the jungle with no leadership. The boy walked north because he could see the sky again through the canopy. His hand felt tight and hot with infection. His fingers turned white first, then red with spreading poison. On the fifth day of walking he gnawed them off to stop the rot.

The seventh day he lost one sandal to the terrain. He threw the other away for balance. In a fit of madness he stripped off his clothes believing they weighed him down. The forest became thinner as he traveled. He was burnt by the sun without protection. There was no water to drink, no food to sustain him. Once he saw a golden eagle and followed it hoping it would lead to prey. But there was no eagle, only his mind playing tricks. On the ninth day he found a man hung from a tree by enemy forces or deserters.

The boy stripped the body of clothes without ceremony. He dressed himself in the garments of the dead man.

As he walked north his hand leaked blood constantly. His feet cramped and trembled with each step on the hard ground. One night he built a fire for warmth despite his fear. It started a great terror in him of attracting the creature. He was brave enough to put his hand inside the flames and stop the rot from spreading further. A small lamp burned steadily on the polished desk. The human wore a pair of thin spectacles on the edge of his nose. Stacks of parchment occupied a far corner of the work surface. He read through pages at a time, scribbling notes on another sheet. Empty ink bottles on the floor suggested the man was rather busy.

From the entrance, Ronn readied his flail, letting the heavy chains dangle, their echoes filling the room. The man refused to look up at the intruders. Instead, he held up a finger and continued reading. Ronn and the rest of his group exchanged glances and shrugged shoulders. They stood still, uncertain how to proceed with such an indifferent target. With a disappointed smack of the tongue, the man replaced the parchment. He pushed his glasses closer to his eyes. Finally, he called for his guests to approach.

"Apologies, my friends," he said. His voice cracked slightly as though it had gone unpracticed for some time. The words came out raspy and uneven.

The adventurers stepped forward slowly. Wilm's head darted around as he scouted for suspicious stones in the floor. He also searched for any sign of another tripwire. The cobbles turned to green when the tasseled edge of the rug stood before them.

"Come," the man muttered, his tone betraying no impatience whatsoever.

Firrel's boot tested its weight against the rug. There was solid ground beneath, which reassured him. The rest followed suit, each placing tentative feet on the fabric.

"Wait!" the man screamed. The group wasted no time assuming a defensive stance. Their weapons and shields were drawn in an instant. "I meant the carpet," he clarified with obvious distress.

The adventurers looked towards their feet. The jade fibers assumed a purplish hue as the blood from their persons dripped freely. Querth's face flushed with embarrassment at the realization.

"Sorry," the wizard whispered.

The man rolled his eyes in exasperation. "It's already ruined beyond repair. Nothing we can do now will restore it. Let's just get this over with as quickly as possible."

The adventurers were finally within a pace of the desk when the open palm of the man begged their halt. The hordes of evil creatures had led them to that chamber through brutal combat. The supposed throne room of unspeakable villainy was little more than a study with a librarian.

"Well, then. I suppose congratulations are in order!" The man clapped his hands together with hollow enthusiasm. "Smashing job on defeating my forces. I'm Pollock and I'll be handling your processing from here."

"Processing?" Edmund echoed in confusion.

"Yes," replied Pollock. "You're almost done in this dreadful castle. Soon you'll be on your way back home to enjoy the spoils. All that's left is to handle the last odds and ends of bureaucracy."

The adventurers nodded in content. They kept their weapons handy nonetheless, unwilling to lower their guard completely. The legions they had to cut through in order to reach that chamber began to feel concluded at last.

"Excellent! Let's get started with the accounting. In total you've slaughtered one hundred and fifty three goblins. You also killed twenty nine orcs during your incursion. Eighteen kobolds fell to your blades as well. Two dragons met their end at your hands, which is quite impressive indeed."

Edmund smirked and rolled the handle of his axe to catch the light. Ronn and Dismal groaned at this display of vanity. They had enjoyed the chaos that had followed as it stopped their fellow warrior from gloating endlessly.

"In addition, you broke down forty one doors throughout the castle. You set off two fire traps during your exploration. Six spike snares were triggered by your careless footsteps. Three boulders were released from their mechanisms. One acid spill was activated in the eastern corridor. Plus, it says you freed the dungeons of ten prisoners who were being held captive."

"All in a day's work," Wilm interjected with pride.

"Quite," responded Pollock, not the least impressed by their boasting. "And adding up your little adventure with standard rates applied, that comes to a total of eight million, eight hundred thirty seven thousand, two hundred and fifty one gold pieces in damages."

Even Querth's mind could not comprehend such a figure despite his mathematical training. They were used to generous spoils from their adventures. Several hundred was the most any had ever seen in a single haul.

"We couldn't possibly carry that much coin," Dismal remarked. "Or spend it in ten lifetimes."

"That's quite expected," Pollock laughed without warmth. "You can just pay in installments over the coming decades."

"Pay?" shouted Firrel in disbelief. "What do you mean pay for our heroic deeds?"

"Your fines for the damages you've caused. You can't just go around killing things indiscriminately. Damaging property costs money to repair. Setting off traps requires professional calibration by skilled technicians."

"But we were on a quest," pleaded Ronn desperately. "We were trying to save the village from your tyranny."

"I see," sneered Pollock with contempt. "Does that mean the village is going to pay the fines for you? Will they rebuild the castle at their expense? Can they reset the protections with their own labor? Who will mop the floors clean of blood? Will your village rehire the guards I employed? Can they retrain dragons from hatchlings? Who will inform the families of those lost in your rampage?" The group stood in wide-eyed silence at these questions. "I didn't think so."

"B-but, it was a quest," Ronn repeated weakly.

"Do you have a license for adventuring? Was there a Writ of Pacification for this 'quest' of yours issued by proper authorities?" Ronn shook his head in defeat. "No need to answer, I already know you don't possess one. If you had bothered to apply for one through the proper channels, this castle would have been better protected by legal wards. Then I wouldn't have been needed to clean up after you. Just a little '[WP]' at the start would have been enough to save us all the mess. Your unauthorized rampage has created a nightmare of paperwork."

"Who was supposed to file our WP?" Querth asked the group with dawning horror. They considered the question for a moment before turning to face /u/dismaldreamer with accusing eyes. "You've ruined us financially!"

"I'm sorry," cried Dismal in genuine anguish. "I didn't know about the licensing requirements! I didn't know this would happen to us!"

The circle closed around him menacingly. The group looked to dispatch their greatest foe: the enemy within their own ranks.
